track: Fact-check: "Capture-based photorealism for a walkable Aokigahara on an M2 Air: Gaussian splats, photogrammetry and hybrids in 2026"

checks.claim: Captured splats cannot take the world's sun or exposure. RealityKit (macOS 27): 'Scene lighting doesn't affect a Gaussian splat asset', with only a spherical grounding shadow. PlayCanvas: splats 'cannot directly receive' shadows; a shadow-catcher mesh is the workaround. GDGS 3.3.0: relighting 'cannot remove light that was baked in', 'Splats do not receive cast shadows', and lighting splats natively costs 2.5–3.9× the frame time. KHR_gaussian_splatting is ratified and display-referred. PlayCanvas splats go through tonemapping by default, and opting out makes them clip and 'look inconsistent'.
checks.source: Apple doc JSON (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/realitykit/gaussiansplatcomponent.json): introducedAt 27.0 on macOS, iOS and visionOS; the quote is verbatim; a spherical proxy grounding shadow; needs the Apple7 GPU family; 'the framework enforces an internal limit on the total number of splats'. The PlayCanvas shadows.md, relighting.md and tonemapping.md pages were fetched and the quotes match. GDGS CHANGELOG 3.3.0 and docs/relighting.md in the scratchpad clone match, including +4.7% for one light and +16% for eight at 271k splats. The KHR README reads 'Complete, Ratified' and says 'scene lighting, exposure settings, and tonemapping generally do not affect rendered splats'.
checks.correction: Nothing to correct. One addition: the KHR spec explicitly allows implementations to relight splats. RealityKit also has an undocumented internal cap on splat count, which the report does not mention.

checks.claim: Godot GDGS 3.3.0 has no LOD, and its only Mac report (issue #2, closed March 2026) showed Metal shader-compile failures, so Godot Metal support is unproven.
checks.source: The scratchpad clone of ReconWorldLab/godot-gaussian-splatting at HEAD (26 Aug 2026) has no LOD code, and its README lists none; the no-LOD part stands. CHANGELOG [2.0.0] 2026-03-18: 'Fixed the macOS and Metal blank-render issue by pre-sizing indirect dispatch dimensions on the CPU'. That is the same day issue #2 was opened, and the release commit is titled 'mac fix'. CHANGELOG [3.1.0]: 'Fixed push-constant alignment for Godot 4.7', and the issue itself reported a push-constant size mismatch. [3.2.0-beta] added a Raster backend that uses Godot's standard pipeline with no compute.
checks.correction: The maintainer shipped fixes aimed at exactly the Mac failures in the issue: the blank render in 2.0.0 and push-constant alignment in 3.1.0. A backend that avoids compute entirely has also existed since July 2026. The accurate status is 'fixes claimed, not independently verified on an M2'. The report's wording, 'showed Metal shader failures', understates this. The lack of LOD still rules GDGS out for trail-length streaming.

checks.claim: The M2 Air can plausibly draw 1–3 M splats in about 6–15 ms, 'about 1–1.5 M splats beside the mesh forest'. The claim rests on PlayCanvas benchmark figures: M4 Max 1–4 M in 6.5–7.4 ms and 35 M in 13.2 ms (WebGL2 75.4 ms), iPhone 13 Pro Max 1–4 M in 12.9–23.6 ms, and Grace Cathedral budgets of 3.5 M desktop and 1.4 M mobile within 400 m.
checks.source: The raw source of playcanvas/blog src/components/GSplatPerfChart/index.jsx matches every figure exactly. M4 Max WebGPU: [7.21, 6.51, 7.38, 6.85 … 13.20]; WebGL2 at 35 M: 75.41. iPhone WebGPU: [12.88, 13.66, 18.96, 23.60]. The Grace Cathedral post matches: 400 m streamed LOD, 3.5 M desktop, 1.4 M mobile. docs/ENGINE_SELECTION.md gives the M2 as 2.9 TFLOPS and 100 GB/s, fanless, with a 30 fps cap and MetalFX at 0.67 scale.
checks.correction: The source numbers are right; the M2 figure is an unmeasured extrapolation and its low end looks optimistic. The M4 Max 1–4 M times are flat at about 7 ms, which is an overhead floor and says nothing about how cost scales with splat count. The A15 phone test ran at only 0.72 MP. MetalFX at 0.67 of the Air's 2560×1664 panel is about 1.9 MP internal, 2.6× the phone test's pixels, while the M2 has only about 2–3× the phone's GPU. A more defensible range is roughly 8–20 ms for 1–3 M splats before throttling. Against the plan's 33 ms (30 fps) budget, that is 25–60% of the frame before the unmeasured Godot or PlayCanvas forest is drawn.

checks.claim: Vegetation is the hardest case even on held-out views, about 5 dB PSNR below indoor scenes. gsplat at 30k: bicycle 25.22/0.764/0.172, stump 26.53/0.768/0.153, room 31.36/0.918/0.164, bonsai 32.06/0.941/0.132.
checks.source: gsplat docs/source/tests/eval.rst (fetched). The quoted rows are exact. The same table also has garden 27.32 / 0.865 / LPIPS 0.075, kitchen 31.16 / 0.926 / 0.094 and counter 29.02 / 0.907 / 0.154.
checks.correction: The report cherry-picks. Garden, the most vegetation-heavy scene, has the best LPIPS of all seven scenes (0.075). Stump's LPIPS (0.153) is better than room's (0.164). The 5 dB gap is PSNR only; in unbounded outdoor scenes PSNR is pulled down by distant background, and it is not a perceptual measure. Mip-NeRF 360 test views are every eighth frame of the same orbit, not 'along the capture path' of a walk. Vegetation is harder, but these numbers do not show it failing perceptually near the capture.

checks.claim: Off the path, quality collapses: DriveSplat reports StreetGS FID 38.3, 61.9 and 149.6 at 1, 2 and 5 m sideways shifts.
checks.source: arxiv.org, huggingface.co and Semantic Scholar were blocked or rate-limited, and the PDF download through export.arxiv.org returned HTTP 406. The export.arxiv.org abstract for 2508.15376 confirms the paper (DriveSplat, Waymo/KITTI) but does not mention shift FIDs.
checks.correction: The figures could not be checked. Even if they are right, they transfer poorly. They come from forward-facing car cameras on a single trajectory, whereas the plan is a two-pass walked 360 capture, so the 5 m collapse may overstate the off-path loss. In the other direction, the same source gives FID 38 even at a 1 m shift, which sits awkwardly with the report's 'literally photographic within 1–2 m'.

checks.claim: None of the owner's 13 real photos passes the UE-derived lighting gate: warm highlights 0/13 (B/R 0.59–0.80), black fraction 2/13, exposure key 5/13, sunfleck 7/13, sky peak 12/13, clipping 13/13. So 'the gate encodes the UE5.8 look, not reality'.
checks.source: I re-ran tools/lighting_stats.py on scratchpad/refphotos/U*_1280.jpg (output in scratchpad/fc_refphotos_recheck.json) and checked it against the g–j bands in renders/ue58_baseline/lighting_stats.json. Every count reproduces exactly, and no photo meets more than 2 of the 4 targets. Photo ranges: key 0.0059–0.0268 (median about 0.0097); sunfleck 0.091–0.224; black 0.056–0.221; highlight B/R 0.585–0.797. For comparison, the flat UE frames a–e measure key 0.02–0.04, sunfleck at most 0.03 and black 0.00.
checks.correction: The counts are right; the interpretation goes too far. On three of the four metrics the real photos sit near the valued g–j frames and far from the flat a–e frames. Several misses are marginal, because each target band is just the min–max of four frames: U02 black 0.169 against a 0.17 floor, U09 sunfleck 0.163 against a 0.16 ceiling, U13 key 0.00797, which passes by a hair. The only systematic divergence is warm highlights, a metric that depends on white balance, from cameras with unknown processing. The photos are also 2:1 crops (1280×629), so the tool's 40% sky/ground split falls on different content than in the 1280×800 gate frames. A fairer reading: reality supports g–j's dark key, sunflecks and deep shade, and only the strong warmth may be UE-specific.

checks.claim: The best 5 × 5 km window has 91% Jōgan lava cover, 39.9 km of path-type ways (6.8 km Fujishōji sen, 2.0 km Tokai Nature Trail, 31 km unnamed, 1.2 km access=no) and 15.9 km of road (6.0 km Route 139). A ±10 m corridor covers 0.8% of the plot along 10 km of trail and 3.2% along 40 km.
checks.source: I independently clipped viewer/assets/terrain/study-context.json to the box x −3735 to 1265, z −1804 to 3196. Trails 39.91 km; unnamed 30.99; Fujishōji sen 6.84; 東海自然歩道 2.05 plus 'Tokai Nature Trail' 0.03; access=no 1.22; roads 15.86; Route 139 5.99. The corridor arithmetic is correct. Jōgan cover from shapely shape() with interior rings is 0.849. The report agent's own scratchpad/trails.py used Polygon(coordinates[0]), which drops the 22 holes in one polygon and gives 0.906. A grid search found no 5 km window above about 0.85.
checks.correction: The lava cover of the window is about 85%, not 91%: the 91% ignores the kīpuka holes in the flow polygon. All the path, road and corridor figures stand.

checks.claim: Matching the planned fixed sun (25–35° elevation) allows only about 1 h of capture per clear day in mid-October: 14:00–14:30 JST (azimuth 226–233°), or 08:30–09:00 (127–133°). That gives about 1 km of trail a day, so 10 or more clear days.
checks.source: I computed solar position (NOAA-style) for 35.47° N, 138.62° E on 15 October 2026. Elevation 25–35° falls at about 08:10–09:15 JST (azimuth 122–136°) and about 13:50–14:55 JST (azimuth 220–237°). ENGINE_SELECTION.md specifies a 'fixed afternoon sun' with elevation 25–35°, side- or back-lit.
checks.correction: Each window lasts about 65 minutes, not 30. The stated '14:00–14:30' is only a slice of the window and contradicts the report's own 'about 1 h'. With the afternoon-only constraint, the conclusion of about 1 h, about 1 km a day and 10 or more clear days is roughly right. The report does not mention that during that hour the sun swings about 15° in azimuth and 10° in elevation. A 'sun-matched' capture therefore still bakes in drifting shadows, never one fixed sun.

checks.claim: The MMS road data is colour-true points, not photographs: 3 cm spacing is about 4.4 px at 5 m in a 1470-px, 90° view and reaches 1 px only at about 22 m, so it is convincing only beyond about 20 m.
checks.source: The arithmetic checks out (f = 735 px; 0.03/5 × 735 = 4.4 px; 1 px at 22 m). The rebuild doc on origin/rebuild/measured-2026-09-19 confirms 'roughly 3 cm point spacing, genuine per-point camera RGB' and that runs from different dates are not harmonised. ENGINE_SELECTION.md plans MetalFX at 0.67 scale on the Air.
checks.correction: 1470 is the Air's logical point width, not its render width. At the plan's roughly 1715-px internal width, 3 cm reaches 1 px at about 26 m. At the 2560-px panel it reaches 1 px at about 38 m. 'Convincing beyond about 20 m' is therefore optimistic; about 25–40 m is closer. The 698 MB-per-sheet figure was not checked.

checks.claim: Apple Object Capture area mode runs on any Apple-silicon Mac and handles 'uneven terrain outdoors' and 2.5D surfaces, so lava, moss and roots can be captured from the trail edge and, once delit, become relightable PBR assets. This is the capture that lifts the free-roam world.
checks.source: WWDC24 session 10107 (fetched). It confirms 'uneven terrain outdoors', 'objects that you can't walk all the way around' and '2.5d surfaces'. It also says: 'Areas larger than 6 feet may have reduced mesh and texture quality unless processed at a higher detail level on Mac'. On-device capture needs iPhone 12 Pro or iPad Pro 2021 and later. Apple advises capturing in diffuse light ('cloudy days or fully shaded areas'). The session says nothing about delighting.
checks.correction: Area mode is meant for patches of about 2 m. Object Capture does not delight. Its textures keep the capture light, which is why Apple asks for overcast conditions, so 'once delit' hides a separate manual or third-party step. Whether the owner has a LiDAR iPhone or iPad is unknown. The recommendation is sound as ground-asset photogrammetry, but it does not fix the trees, which the decision record names as the fidelity cap.

omissions: The hardware ceiling is never stated. The M2 Air's 8-core GPU gives about 2.9 TFLOPS and 100 GB/s, fanless, according to ENGINE_SELECTION.md. That is roughly one twenty-eighth of an RTX 4090's compute and one tenth of its bandwidth. Free-roam photorealism in dense forest is out of reach on this machine whatever the engine or capture. A hardware change (an M4/M5 Max Mac, or an RTX PC, where NVIDIA-only splat shadowing and neural rendering become options) would change the answer more than any capture trip.

For the recommended 'on-rails trail walk' mode, plain 8K 360 video from the X6 is literally photographic. It needs no training, no SfM on 260k frames, no CUDA rental and no splat runtime, and plays trivially on the M2. Splats add only 1–2 m of parallax on top. The report never compares the two, and that comparison could remove most of the capture pipeline cost.

The non-interactive route (P6 in the decision record) is left out. Path-traced stills or flythroughs in Blender Cycles, or rendered splat videos, can get much closer to photoreal on this Mac than any real-time path. For an owner asking 'can it be photoreal', that is the one route where the answer is closer to yes.
The report never asks the owner which kind of 'photorealistic' he means. It could mean photoreal stills, photoreal on rails, or photoreal free roam, and the answer differs sharply for each.

The trees are what the decision record says caps fidelity, and the report does not address them. It covers ground-asset photogrammetry and bark and needle textures, but not what species-accurate Tsuga and Chamaecyparis trees would take, or whether foliage capture works at all. So it never answers whether the synthetic 97–99% of the plot could move towards photoreal.

The gate's target bands are just the min–max of four UE frames. The report does not say how narrowly the photos miss (for example black 0.169 against 0.17). That matters for its own recommendation to rebase the gate on calibrated photos.

Frame budget context is missing. The plan targets 30 fps (33 ms), not 60, which changes how much room a 1–3 M splat corridor leaves. The Godot forest's own M2 frame time is unmeasured, so the combined budget is unknown.

RealityKit has an undocumented internal splat-count limit, and PlayCanvas's distance LOD is already the default in 2.22.4. Both are minor, but the report's advice to 'set distance LOD explicitly' is unnecessary.
overall:
The headline survives the checks: capture could look photographic only in small, fixed places, and a free-roam 5 × 5 km world on this M2 Air will not be photoreal. Most facts it cites check out exactly: the gsplat table, the RealityKit doc (macOS 27, no scene lighting), the PlayCanvas shadow, relighting and tonemapping docs, the PlayCanvas perf chart, the Grace Cathedral budgets, the GDGS 3.3.0 relighting limits, the KHR spec, the OSM path lengths and the gate counts for the photos, which I reproduced.

The errors are secondary but lean in both directions.

**Too pessimistic in places:**
- It says 'the gate encodes UE5.8, not reality'. In fact the real photos sit near the valued g–j frames on three of four metrics and miss mainly on white-balance-sensitive warmth.
- It frames vegetation as the weakest case with PSNR only. On LPIPS, garden scores best of all seven scenes.
- It understates GDGS on the Mac. The maintainer shipped Mac and Metal fixes in 2.0.0 and 3.1.0, plus a backend with no compute.

**Too optimistic in places:**
- The low end of the M2 splat cost (6 ms) ignores the roughly 1.9 MP MetalFX internal resolution.
- The 'convincing beyond about 20 m' figure for MMS uses 1470 logical points; at render resolution it is about 25–40 m.
- 'Once delit' photogrammetry skips a step Apple does not provide.

**Plain errors:**
- The lava cover of the window is about 85%, not 91%: the report agent's script dropped the polygon holes.
- The afternoon sun window is about 13:50–14:55, not 14:00–14:30.
- The DriveSplat off-path figures are unverifiable here.

The biggest gaps are omissions that bear directly on the owner's question. The report never names the M2's hardware ceiling as the root cause, and never says that a hardware change would matter more than capture. It never notes that plain 360 video already gives a literally photographic on-rails mode at a fraction of the splat pipeline's cost. It also ignores the offline route, where photoreal is most attainable on this Mac.

The honest short answer to 'can this achieve photorealistic fidelity?' is:
- **Free roam on this Mac:** no.
- **On rails:** yes, most cheaply as 360 video.
- **Stills or offline renders:** closer to yes than the report suggests.
